confidence_notes: I based the restaurant and coffee anchors on searches of aggregated cost-of-living sites. Expatica and Numbeo put an inexpensive meal at about EUR 15.60–18, a mid-range dinner for two at about EUR 71–72, a cappuccino at about EUR 1.80–1.90 and a domestic draft pint at about EUR 6. A smaller standard serving was set a little lower, at about EUR 5.50. The sources were collected at different times and their figures differ, so the anchors are rounded to typical July levels. Cocktail prices conflicted: one crowd-sourced figure was about EUR 6 from 7 price points, while one cocktail bar's listing was about USD 12. I picked about EUR 9, which fits typical Italian bar prices relative to beer. I found no wine-by-the-glass price, so wine is estimated at about EUR 5 from its usual price relationship to beer. Accommodation anchors are general model estimates for July high season, not checked against live listings. Pisa has only a few hostels and is a day-trip and airport hub, so hostel anchors are less certain. Euros were converted to US dollars at about 1.10 USD per EUR, calculated from the RBA rates of 0.6720 USD and 0.6115 EUR per AUD.
comparable_city_reasoning: Pisa is a mid-sized Tuscan university city with heavy day-trip tourism. I compared it to Lucca and Bologna, where prices are somewhat below Florence, but summer hotel rates are pushed up by visitors to the Leaning Tower and travellers using the airport.
